title: Kobi <> Cedrick - Daily Standup - 2026/08/18 10:29 EDT - Notes by Gemini
screen_reason: Internal standup with WagerTech delivery content: timeline change to a full November go-live, scope expansion to CMS integration, Phase 1 live-website testing milestone, file-storage POC approach (internal-first, GCP/service account access), and proof deletion/replacement edge cases.

items.topic: Three phases dropped; full go-live November
items.statement: Kobi reported that the project moved away from the original three phases. WagerTech wants to go live with everything on November 1 (full go-live in the first week of November) instead of mid-August.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: they've kind of we moved away from like the three phases that we initially had to um in our last meeting uh they basically wanted to go live November 1st with everything. / Kobi Kunasekaran: So, they are a little behind on that. So, um, let's see how that goes. But, uh, as of now, the plan is like we're no longer going live mid August. It's already mid August. Um, we're planning to do like a full go live uh first week of November.
items.supersedes_hint: Replaces the original three-phase plan and the mid-August go-live.
items.note: Reported second hand by Kobi (client decision made 'in our last meeting'); not decided in this meeting. Gemini Summary line 16 frames it as 'The major decision finalized' here; Details line 47 matches the transcript.

items.topic: Scope expanded beyond sign-up logging to CMS
items.statement: Kobi reported that Phase 1 was originally only the sign-up logging experience. WagerTech then wanted to integrate Salesforce with their CMS for deal management and rep management at the same time, and Kobi said this makes sense.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Yeah. Like initially we said, you know, we'll we'll do the just a signup logging experience which was supposed to be phase one and then we'll start adding other things on top later. But then they wanted to do like they wanted to integrate Salesforce with their CMS for the whole deal management / Kobi Kunasekaran: rep and rep management piece which honestly it makes sense.
items.supersedes_hint: Earlier plan: Phase 1 = sign-up logging only, other items added later.
items.note: Reported second hand by Kobi. 'deal management rep and rep management' kept as transcribed.

items.topic: Next milestone: test Phase 1 with live website
items.statement: Kobi said the next milestone is to get everything built in Phase 1 fully tested with WagerTech's live website. The plan for this week was to connect their agency website so clicks and live data come into the Sandbox.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: they've kind of we moved away from like the three phases that we initially had to um in our last meeting uh they basically wanted to go live November 1st with everything. So, um, we're still like I think the the main the first milestone or actually the next milestone is to get the, uh, everything that we built in phase one fully tested uh, with their like live website. Um, so that that was the plan for this week is to hook up their agency website so we can start getting some clicks um, and live data coming in through in Sandbox.

items.statement: Kobi said WagerTech is a little behind on connecting the website for live Sandbox data.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: So, they are a little behind on that. So, um, let's see how that goes. / Cedrick Infantado: they they are far behind the schedule if if the go live is November.

items.topic: Earlier custom LWC UI work deleted
items.statement: Kobi said the earlier work done on WagerTech's side (a fully custom LWC Lightning UI for sign-up logging) was deleted because it did not support the actual process. The current build is less polished visually but more usable and practical.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: We we ended up like deleting all of that work. They they spent most of their time on like a custom UI like fully custom LWC lightning pages / Kobi Kunasekaran: but it's far more usable and far more practical.

items.topic: Proof deletion and replacement edge cases
items.statement: Cedrick raised edge cases not covered in the project document, for example what happens on deletion or replacement when a new proof is uploaded. Kobi said the client did not raise these, Jumpr needs to bring them up with the client, and a plan can follow later; they are outside the MVP/happy path for the POC.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: They're actually really good questions and I don't think we address them in the document. So, I do want to make sure uh we cover those scenarios like the especially with like you know what do we do for deletion replacements if they want to upload like a new proof. those are edge cases that the client obviously didn't raise. Um, but those are things that, you know, we need to bring up for them. / Cedrick Infantado: Because on my mind right now we're just focusing on the PC and that those information can come later.

items.statement: Kobi and Cedrick agreed to build the file-storage POC integration in Jumpr's own environment first, to keep control and find challenges, then give WagerTech final instructions later. This is internal Jumpr alignment only; the client has not accepted it and access still had to be checked.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Uh part of me wants to do the internal version first because at least that way we can also kind of figure out / Kobi Kunasekaran: Yeah. And we have control, right? Like we can see like what problems they might run into and anticipate. So uh I'm thinking we still go with that approach and then if there are any changes and tweaks that we need to make, we can do all of that and then give them uh the final instructions later. / Cedrick Infantado: That would be great. So, um maybe we can finalize that we will use internal first uh for for at least the / Cedrick Infantado: PO. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Okay. Yeah, it's a good idea.
items.note: Firmness held at proposed: agreement is between two Jumpr team members, not confirmed with WagerTech, and depends on getting account access.

items.topic: GCP account choice depends on timing
items.statement: The POC needs access to a Google Cloud (GCP) account or service account, either WagerTech's or Jumpr's, to start the integration and Apex calls. Kobi said if WagerTech is not ready when Cedrick needs access, Jumpr will use its own account; if WagerTech provides the information by end of week, WagerTech's account will be used. The project document's POC requirements section lists what Jumpr needs from WagerTech.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: like we need to get access to uh some sort of like Google like either wager tax or our own Google uh Google service cl Google sorry GCP accounts uh or like a service account to get the integration going and start setting up like the Apex calls and things like that. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Uh, I think it depends on timing. So, like if you tell me, you know, you're ready to get started and you need access to the account tomorrow, um if Wager Tech is not ready, um I'll reach out to Wed and we'll access to our account. Um, but if it's going to be like closer to the end of the week and Wet Techch uh is able to get us all the information by then, then we'll just use Wayext account, right?
items.asr_note: wager tax / Wet Techch / Wayext = WagerTech [ASR]; Wed = likely a Jumpr person who controls the Jumpr account [ASR?]; PLC requirement section (line 158) = POC requirements [ASR?]

items.statement: Cedrick estimated he could start on the POC on Thursday and wants account access by then.
items.quote: Cedrick Infantado: yeah, I remember that part. So uh I'll just check it again so that uh um I can verify all of the information all right uh for that one but um from uh from my perspective I'm thinking about Thursday I could already start with u the P um uh so it's better to have the access by then

items.topic: Kobi to check access for POC setup
items.statement: Kobi will check later that day whether Jumpr can get access to set up the POC environment.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: so I can I can check with them and see if we can get access to set all of this / Kobi Kunasekaran: up.

items.topic: Kobi to set up service accounts
items.statement: Kobi will do the Google service account setup to get Cedrick going and record the steps for later reuse.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: That's fine. like I've I've set up like service accounts and stuff before. So, / Kobi Kunasekaran: I can I can probably do the setup uh to get you going and then um we'll I'll I'll try and make sure to remember to record everything so that we know how to do it later.

items.topic: External file storage instead of Salesforce
items.statement: Kobi described the strategy as using an external service to store files because the client does not want to store files in Salesforce. No native Salesforce integration was found, so it may need to be built from scratch.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Uh but quick question like I I know like in terms of what we're trying to do, right? Like from a strategy perspective um you know essentially all we're trying to do is use an external service to store files. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Like I don't think anybody on our end has built anything like that. I was really hoping Salesforce would have some sort of integration, but uh I like we weren't able to find anything.
items.note: Kobi's internal restatement of existing scope; no client confirmation in this meeting.

items.statement: Kobi asked Cedrick to suggest alternatives (including an easier existing integration) once he understands the nature of the files being uploaded; Jumpr can pivot if an easier way exists.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: I don't know if you've gotten that far in the videos but once you kind of see the nature of the files and things that they're uploading uh let me know if you have any alternate suggestions. / Cedrick Infantado: Okay, sure.

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: Decisions / Aligned: Internal build chosen for POC The team will develop the internal version of the proof-of-concept first to maintain control and proactively identify integration challenges before involving the client's infrastructure.
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Cedrick Infantado: That would be great. So, um maybe we can finalize that we will use internal first uh for for at least the / Cedrick Infantado: PO. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Okay. Yeah, it's a good idea.
gemini_disagreements.why: Summary presents this as an aligned decision. In the transcript it is internal agreement between two Jumpr team members, with access still to be checked and no client acceptance; firmness held at proposed.

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: The major decision finalized the project timeline with a target go-live date of November 1.
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: they've kind of we moved away from like the three phases that we initially had to um in our last meeting uh they basically wanted to go live November 1st with everything.
gemini_disagreements.why: Summary implies the timeline was decided in this meeting. Transcript shows Kobi reporting a client decision from an earlier meeting. Content (November go-live) matches; attribution does not.
